name: Crude oil, fractional distillation and alkanes

terms.definition: A finite resource, a mixture of many hydrocarbons, formed from the remains of plankton buried in mud.
A compound made of hydrogen and carbon atoms only.
terms.examiner: Water is not a hydrocarbon; methane is.

terms.definition: A saturated hydrocarbon with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
Separating crude oil into fractions by heating and condensing them at different temperatures in a column.
terms.examiner: Fractions have similar numbers of carbon atoms.

terms.definition: How thick (resistant to flow) a liquid is; it increases with the size of the molecule.
terms.examiner: Larger molecules: higher boiling point, more viscous, less flammable.

terms.definition: Hydrocarbon + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water, releasing energy.
terms.examiner: Balance the equation with oxygen last.
